name: SDN Host Clock Node
description: Host clock connector (typed contracts 1.0). Method "now" takes an optional "trigger" frame, a TimerTick (TICK, module-sdk runtime type; its payload is not read), samples the host clock through clock.now and clock.nowIso (SDS $PIV hostcalls: a TimeValue record and the raw RFC3339 text) and emits one "time" frame, a $TIM (SDS standard TIM): TIME_SYSTEM UTC with an INSTANT {UTC, EPOCH_FORMAT UNIX_SECONDS, SECONDS whole Unix seconds, SUBSECOND_NANOS the millisecond remainder, ISO8601 the host's RFC3339 reading}. No JSON. PERIODIC emission is a flow TRIGGER concern (timer trigger kind), not this node: wire a timer trigger at the flow level and place this node downstream when a flow needs the sampled time as data. Host gating: the Go node (sdn-server modulert) serves clock.* as ungated built-ins; the SDK NodeHost/BrowserHost are default-deny and require the "clock" capability grant, so this node declares it.

externalInterfaces.description: Host clock hostcalls as SDS $PIV invocations (clock.now -> TimeValue UNIX_MS, clock.nowIso -> raw "value" RFC3339 text). Available on the Go server host (built-in) and SDK NodeHost/BrowserHost (capability-gated).

acceptedTypeSets.description: Optional TimerTick (module-sdk runtime type TICK), e.g. a flow timer trigger's firing. Its fields are not read: any tick causes one clock sample, and an invoke without one samples too.

$TIM (SDS standard TIM): TIME_SYSTEM UTC; INSTANT {TIME_SYSTEM UTC, EPOCH_FORMAT UNIX_SECONDS, SECONDS = floor(clock.now / 1000), SUBSECOND_NANOS = (clock.now mod 1000) * 1e6, ISO8601 = clock.nowIso verbatim}. SECONDS + SUBSECOND_NANOS are clock.now's Unix milliseconds exactly.

outputPorts.description: The sampled host time as one $TIM frame.

methods.description: Samples clock.now and clock.nowIso through the sync typed hostcall bridge (SDS $PIV) and emits both readings in one $TIM frame.

sequentialJustification.detail: Each invocation makes one clock hostcall and answers it on the calling thread; the host runs independent invocations in parallel and this module creates no threads.
